terms.gloss: panes of transparent stone or glass; a glazed frame for plants
evidence: Plin. NH 19.64: intrā speculārium mūnīmenta (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Not a building but the nearest ancient thing: Tiberius’s gardeners grew his cucumbers in beds on wheels, pushed into the sun and in winter drawn back behind panes (Pliny). Morgan–Owens has the heading “greenhouse, hothouse” without a Latin word, and we found none in Traupman. Pliny has the genitive speculārium.

phrases.latin: rūrsusque hībernīs diēbus intrā speculārium mūnīmenta revocantibus
phrases.english: and on winter days drawing them back behind the shelter of the panes
